text:
Chicago came to Raleigh winless in six games (0-5-1) and left having conceded nine, the 9-2 rout by Carolina at Lenovo Center coming against a team that had already beaten them 5-2 on Oct. 10. By the time the Blackhawks scored, the game was long decided. Carolina had seven goals before Roman Kantserov got one back in the third period, and four of them came in the first period alone.

Jordan Martinook, drafted 58th overall by Phoenix in 2012 and the first star on the night, scored twice in that period, once at 10:54 and again at 19:27 to make it 4-0. Seth Jarvis and Jackson Blake had scored in the opening four minutes. Spencer Knight allowed six goals on 17 shots and gave up 3.7 goals more than the quality of those shots would suggest, before Arvid Soderblom took over in a game already gone.

The numbers say Carolina deserved the lopsided scoreboard, if not quite nine goals. We put expected goals, a measure of the quality of chances, at 4.37 for Carolina and 2.32 for Chicago, and in simulated replays of every shot the Hurricanes win 81% of the time. The Hurricanes also outshot Chicago 33-20 and won 28 of 44 faceoffs. Chicago had its best stretch in the third period, when the chances were even at 1.69 apiece, and Connor Bedard added a goal and an assist across Kantserov's goal and his own.

That leaves Chicago with its winless run at six and little to take from the night beyond that third period. Carolina, already ahead of Chicago in the season series, has nothing in our facts to suggest anything other than a very comfortable win.
